subject: Qur'an and Tajweed
statusNote: No National Curriculum or exam-board framework exists for Qur'an and Tajweed. This is the school's own programme, drawn from its lesson files (Reception to Year 9) and the tajweed-by-year layout of the old Drive Quran tracker. Recitation follows the Madinah mushaf, Hafs 'an 'Asim. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. Status Provisional. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics.

sources.title: School Drive Quran folder: TPS Quran Tracker 2020-21 (tajweed-by-year sheet only; pupil data not used)

purpose: To read the Qur'an fluently and accurately from the mushaf with correct tajweed.
To memorise selected surahs securely and keep them through revision.
To understand the meaning of what is recited and to show adab with the Qur'an.
Standard: Arabic script is always shown with transliteration, never transliteration alone.

statements: Learn letters, sounds, short vowels, joining, sukoon, shaddah, madd and tanween.
Read short surahs from the mushaf with support.
Year 2: noon sakinah and tanween rules, qalqalah, ghunnah, meem sakinah, madd and stopping signs.
Al-Fatihah, An-Nas, Al-Falaq, Al-Ikhlas; Al-'Asr and Al-Kawthar in Year 2.
Know that the Qur'an is Allah's words and learn simple meanings of the surahs.
Say Bismillah correctly and show good manners with the Qur'an.
Begin with isti'adha and basmalah; read stopping signs; refine pace and breath (tarteel).
Heavy and light letters, idgham, madd family, makharij, laam rules, similar letters and letter qualities.
Al-Fil, Quraysh, Al-Kafirun, An-Nasr, Al-Masad, Ad-Duha, Ash-Sharh, At-Tin.
Reflect on the meaning of surahs recited; learn how to memorise and keep what is learned.
Baseline recitation, goals and recital assessments each year.
Makharij, sifat, madd system, noon and meem rules in full, meeting letters, waqf and ibtida', alif-lam and hamzat al-wasl.
Al-Qadr (Y7), Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur (Y8), Al-'Asr, Al-Humazah and Al-Fil (Y9).
Meaning, reflection (tadabbur) and lessons from each surah studied.

toKS4: There is no Qur'an qualification at KS4 in this pack. Year 10 and 11 lesson files continue the programme (Ayat al-Kursi 2:255, Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4, Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-10) and support Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies (4IS1), whose set passages (for example 97:1-5, 112:1-4, 2:183-185) are studied in Arabic and English. Qur'an lessons give recitation and meaning for these passages in sections 1.2, 2.1 and 3.3.

links.topic: Meaning and tafsir of the surahs recited
links.how: Qur'an lessons build recitation and memory; Islamic Studies explains the meaning and context.
Learning about Hira and revelation gives context for reciting the Qur'an.
Shared letter knowledge helps both; Arabic adds grammar and vocabulary, Qur'an adds tajweed.
Words met in surahs (such as ayah, rabb) are used in Arabic lessons.
Learning letter-sound links in Arabic mirrors phonics habits taught in English.
Pace, breath and voice in tarteel connect with reading aloud and performance.
Science teaches how sound is produced; makharij lessons apply this to letter articulation.

links.topic: Memory, revision cycles and study habits
links.how: Spaced revision and self-assessment skills support memorisation and general study.

links.topic: Preservation and compilation of the Qur'an
links.how: History source skills support the 4IS1 topic on how the Qur'an was compiled (1.2).

gaps: There is no official framework; the structure is the school's own.

Only the Drive tracker's tajweed-by-year sheet was read; it is a 2020-21 pupil tracker and its pupil data was not used. Its per-year assignments are consistent with the lesson files but were not copied in full.
Memorisation targets are taken from what lesson files say pupils recite and memorise; no formal juz or surah memorisation target by year has been seen.
Reception to Year 2 lessons use Qaidah-style reading; the Drive Qaidah sheets were not opened.
Some surahs recur (Al-Fil in Y3 and Y9, Al-'Asr in Y2 and Y9) as revisit points; confirm this is intended.
Qur'anic references are limited to those named in the lesson files.
